input: Pitch a column idea to a local newspaper

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Whether this is a recurring column or a one-off piece changes the pitch structure, commitment level, and what the editor needs to evaluate.
Knowing who the target audience of the column is shapes the angle, tone, and how the pitch frames its value to the newspaper.
The specific newspaper and its editorial focus determines what style, topics, and pitch format are appropriate.
A hard deadline — such as a submission window or a news hook that expires — directly affects how quickly and in what order tasks must be done.
The column topic and the user's unique angle or voice is the core of the pitch; without it, no plan can be built around the actual content.
Understanding what the user considers a successful outcome — a reply, a meeting, a published sample — defines what the pitch needs to achieve.
Whether the user has an existing contact at the paper or is reaching out cold changes the channel, format, and tone of the pitch entirely.

gold.taskTitle: Pitch a column idea to a local newspaper
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to pitch a recurring or one-off column concept to a local newspaper and needs a plan to do it effectively.

questions.title: Is this a recurring column or a single piece?
questions.description: Clarify whether the user is pitching an ongoing column with a regular cadence or a standalone feature article, as this changes the pitch structure significantly.

questions.title: Who is the intended audience for your column?
questions.description: Identify the specific readership the column is aimed at (e.g. local parents, small business owners, retirees) to shape the pitch's value proposition.

questions.title: Which specific newspaper are you targeting?
questions.description: Name the publication so the plan can account for its editorial style, existing columns, submission guidelines, and local focus.

questions.title: Do you have a deadline or time-sensitive news hook?
questions.description: Determine whether there is a hard submission date or a topical hook that expires, which would set the pace and priority of the entire plan.

questions.title: What is the topic and your unique angle on it?
questions.description: Capture the core subject matter and the specific perspective or expertise the user brings that differentiates this column from what the paper already publishes.

questions.title: What does a successful pitch outcome look like to you?
questions.description: Clarify whether success means getting a reply, securing an in-person meeting, having a sample piece published, or landing a formal column agreement.

questions.title: Do you already have a contact at the newspaper?
questions.description: Establish whether the user is pitching to a known editor or reaching out cold, which determines the channel, format, and tone of the pitch.
